entry: Yanjie Ze, Gu Zhang, Kangning Zhang, Chenyuan Hu, Muhan Wang, and Huazhe Xu. 3d diffusion policy. arXiv preprint arXiv:2403.03954, 2024.
contexts: While existing works incorporating depth into DP often rely on dedicated sensors to capture real-time depth data [46, 24], we aim to explore a more lightweight and efficient approach without adding hardware complexity or additional costs.
content:
We need to decide if reference [46] (3D Diffusion Policy) supports FastUMI's claim: "While existing works incorporating depth into DP often rely on dedicated sensors to capture real-time depth data [46, 24], we aim to explore a more lightweight and efficient approach without adding hardware complexity or additional costs."

So FastUMI uses [46] to support that existing works incorporating depth into DP rely on dedicated sensors to capture real-time depth data. Does 3D Diffusion Policy rely on dedicated sensors? In the cited paper, they use a RealSense L515 camera to obtain depth images. That's a dedicated depth sensor. They also mention "We use one RealSense L515 camera to obtain real-world visual observations." So yes, they rely on a dedicated depth sensor. The claim is about "existing works incorporating depth into DP often rely on dedicated sensors to capture real-time depth data". The cited paper does use a RealSense L515 depth camera. So it supports the claim that depth-based DP uses dedicated sensors. However, the claim says "often rely" and cites [46] as an example. The paper indeed uses a RealSense L515. So supported.

Need quote from cited paper: "We use one RealSense L515 camera to obtain real-world visual observations." That's verbatim. Also maybe "For both simulation and the real world, we obtain depth images with size 84 × 84 from a single camera." But the sensor mention is clear.

Thus status supported. Provide claim, quote, reason.

parsed.reason: The cited paper explicitly states that it uses a RealSense L515 depth camera to obtain visual observations, confirming that this depth-based diffusion policy work relies on a dedicated depth sensor, which supports FastUMI's characterization.
